searches.note: Twenty six searches of a share of twenty eight, none of them the author's; two left unspent. Six were restricted to a primary body's or a house's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: emidiopepe.com (the decanting sheet and the method), masciarelli.it twice (the family and winery pages; the Villa Gemma sheets and page), illuminativini.com twice (the Zanna page; the history page) and cataldimadonna.com (the cantina page). Five more searches blocked the author's own sources so that a second, independent source would show: Gambero Rosso and Doctor Wine for Dino Illuminati, Decanter and WineNews for Gianni Masciarelli, Gambero Rosso for Luigi Cataldi Madonna, the house for Piè delle Vigne and Zanna, three merchants for Valentini's casks. One WebFetch was tried, the Villa Gemma English sheet on www.masciarelli.it, and refused (the host does not resolve here); no other fetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept in a record marked checked.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification and its year, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the bodies' own texts (the consorzio's Trebbiano d'Abruzzo, Colline Teramane and Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo texts) and the houses' own pages for their own dates and methods, then to the press and the merchants, with the author's sources blocked where they would only have repeated themselves, for the second source of each date, person and place.

Where a detail rested on no source the refuter read (the two years in bottle for Zanna, the business trip, at home, the birthday) it was cut; where the sources corrected the record (Pepe's decanting into a new bottle, Masciarelli's steel since 2012, the Giulia IGT, the death of Luigi Cataldi Madonna) the record was set right with its source.

Sources whose title or address names a living person, or that are a writer's own site, were read in the results and never cited: an interview with a granddaughter of Emidio Pepe, two magazine profiles of Masciarelli's partner and daughter, a regional government page whose address names a living councillor, and two wine blogs.

tested: The family at Loreto Aprutino since the seventeenth century, from 1650 by one account: merchants' pages in the results give 1650 and the mid 1600s beside Fine and Rare Wines: confirmed as written.

Edoardo Valentini, his death in 2006 at 72 and the law he gave up in the 1950s to return home: Fine and Rare Wines and IT Wine Club, with other merchants' pages in the results (the law and the return home in two of them), and WineNews on the park in Rome named for him: confirmed; no birth year found, so he keeps his death alone. His son's taking on of the estate: confirmed; the son is living and unnamed.

The DOC of 1972 and the label's at least 85 per cent: the consorzio's text gives the DPR of 28 June 1972 and Trebbiano Abruzzese and/or Trebbiano Toscano at a minimum of 85 per cent, as modified by the DM of 19 January 2023; Federdoc's older listing also admits Bombino Bianco, which the current text no longer names: confirmed as written.
The grape, Trebbiano Abruzzese rather than Toscano: a merchant in the results (the Trebbiano Abruzzese clone) beside the author's Vinous: confirmed.

The large old oak casks: Signorvino and Enoteca Gambi give about a year in large oak casks, one of them Slavonian casks some over seventy years old, with no barrique: confirmed; the library's old large wood agrees. The pergola abruzzese is on two merchants' pages and Vinous, and is left for the integrator (the five sources are full).

The house rules: no living person named (the son, his wife and their son, and the Roman officials of the park met and not named), no price (merchant prices read and not used), no score (Guida Espresso's marks read and not used), nothing volatile (the hectares, 60 or 65, left out), no judging superlative, British, no dash. The cards and questions: the missing vintage question has one key the library teaches, and its distractors are four reasons of one kind; the law question's four careers are plausible and the explanation teaches.
open: Training is still left out of the sites: the pergola abruzzese is now on Vinous's vertical (the author's reading) and on two Italian merchants' pages the refuter read (Enoteca Gambi, Pedrelli), which would be two sources, but the record's five sources are full and the field reads true without it; the integrator may add it.
Edoardo Valentini's birth year is still in no source read: Fine and Rare Wines gives his death in 2006 at 72, so 1933 or 1934, and he keeps his death alone.
The ageing in large casks is about a year on two merchants' pages and six to twelve months on another; the record gives no length, which stands.

tested: The founder's dates: Sky TG24 (born to a farming family in 1932, the estate founded in 1964), Adnkronos in Il Foglio and Vinous (died 28 July 2026 at 94): confirmed; the birthday the day before and the place of death not shown, cut.

The making: the house's method page (destemmed by hand on a net over a wooden vat, the berries falling through), Vinous (by hand through a wire mesh; many of the 25 to 30 hectolitre glass lined cement tanks those of 1964), merchants' pages in the results (the white grapes for the Trebbiano trodden by foot): confirmed as written.
The decanting: the house's Epoca di decantazione sheet and method page, read through search on its own domain: corrected (into a new bottle, a new cork with the year, the red only).
The family: daughters at the helm with granddaughters beside them (Sky TG24): corrected to the plural; all living and unnamed.
The DOC on the label: vino.com lists the red as Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC, with the library: confirmed.

The house rules: no living person named, no price (the Zachys auction pages read and not used), no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative (one belief of rank cut), British, no dash. The cards and questions: the destemming question's distractors are four ways of handling grapes and the explanation teaches the white's foot treading against the red's net; the year question's 1899 and 1932 are the plausible near misses, both explained.

tested: The founding, the grandfather and 1981: the house's family and winery pages, read through search on its own domain (his maternal grandfather, the company founded in 1981 to make Trebbiano and Montepulciano d'Abruzzo), and Gambero Rosso International (forty years since the first vintage of 1981): confirmed. One heritage page gives a farm at San Martino in 1978 and wine first in 1981; 1981 stands with the library.
The first vintage of 700 bottles of Montepulciano and 1,300 of Trebbiano: the house's press kit: confirmed as the house's account.
Villa Gemma of 1984 and the meeting of 1987: the house's pages (first year of production 1984; met his partner in 1987, a partnership towards growth abroad): confirmed.
Colle Cave: the house's pages, about 400 metres at San Martino sulla Marrucina, clay with medium limestone, facing south and east, Guyot at about 9,000 vines a hectare: confirmed as written.

The making: the house's sheets (twelve months in first passage barriques on the English sheet, eighteen in new ones and at least 24 months in bottle on the Italian sheet of 2019, steel since 2012) and Bottle of Italy for 2018: the steel dated, the rest confirmed. The one fetch of the run, the English sheet on masciarelli.it, was refused: the host does not resolve here.

The death: WineNews (31 July, suddenly, in Munich) and Wine Spectator (31 July 2008, in a clinic in Munich after a cerebral haemorrhage, at 52; others 53): the year and the day confirmed, the business trip cut.

The house rules: his partner and daughter, both living, met and not named (the library's holdings line names the partner); no price, no score (Decanter's and the guides' marks read and not used), nothing volatile, no judging superlative, British, no dash. tested: The founding of 1890: several pages in the results date the house to 1890 and its founder Nicola, called Nicò; the state's heritage catalogue lists a Casa Illuminati of the later nineteenth century at Ripatransone, and Il Centro gives Dino Illuminati's birth there: confirmed beside the house's history page.

The move of 1960 to Controguerra, the farmhouse at Zanna and the wolves: the house's history page, read through search on its own domain (left Ripatransone with his family for Controguerra in 1960; bought a farmhouse and land, five hectares in English and ten in Italian, in an area called Zanna, a name from the wolves that lived there): confirmed as the house's account, the hectares left out.

The DOCG and the Riserva: the consorzio's text (DM of 20 February 2003, Gazzetta Ufficiale of 6 April 2003; a Riserva at least three years, one in wood and two months in bottle; Montepulciano at least 90 per cent): the decree confirmed, the Riserva's meaning confirmed as written.

Zanna: the house's Zanna page (the first historic plot, 280 metres, marl and clay, 100 per cent Montepulciano, steel at no more than 30 degrees, the malolactic before the wood, made only in the best years) and five merchants' sheets (24 to 26 months in 25 hectolitre Slavonian casks): confirmed, save the two years in bottle, cut.
Dino Illuminati's death: AbruzzoWeb, Il Pescara, Virtù Quotidiane, Il Messaggero and Il Centro (15 February 2023, at 92): confirmed; at home cut.

The house rules: the founder's living namesake and the sons met and not named, nor the consortium's president quoted in the obituaries; no price, no score, nothing volatile (the 110 to 130 hectares left out), no judging superlative, British, no dash. The cards and questions: the appellation question's distractors are four real or plausible names of one kind, the explanation teaching Controguerra DOC against the DOCG; the wolves question's key is the house's own and the fang shaped bend is answered by the meaning of zanna.

tested: The history: the house's cantina page, read through search on its own domain (the baron in 1920, his son Antonio first bottling in 1975, the Warrior of Capestrano on the label from that year, found a few metres from the vineyards, the grandson Luigi from 1990, grapes certified organic from 2016): confirmed as the house's account; the obituaries of Luigi Cataldi Madonna give the grandfather the baron, 1920 and 1990 independently.

Luigi Cataldi Madonna: Gambero Rosso, Askanews, Il Centro, AbruzzoLive, Il Pescara and Chieti Today (died 8 December 2025 at 69; a professor at L'Aquila; the estate from his father around 1990): his death added, his relation to the bottler borne out.

Piè delle Vigne: merchants' pages in the results, Clickwine, Vicino and Italian Wine Selection among those listed (first made in 1997 by the svacata, red vinification added to a white ferment as the farmers once did; about a year in steel and a year in bottle): confirmed as written; one merchant's 2007 as the first vintage without wood and another's 85 and 15 per cent left out.

Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo: the consorzio's text (a type of Montepulciano d'Abruzzo by DPR of 24 May 1968; its own DOC by DM of 5 October 2010; a Superiore type) and the eAmbrosia file (DM of 5 October 2010): confirmed as written.

Ofena and the Forno d'Abruzzo: Quotidiano Nazionale (320 to 440 metres in a basin called the oven of Abruzzo for its heat by day) and a page of Masciarelli's on the province of L'Aquila (the Gran Sasso stops the sea breeze): confirmed.
Giulia and Supergiulia, Tonì: corrected for the IGT; Tonì in 25 hectolitre casks on a merchant's page beside the house's: confirmed.

The house rules: the daughter now at the helm met and not named, the late son described; no price, no score (Gambero Rosso's award not used), nothing volatile (the 30 or 31 hectares left out), no judging superlative, British, no dash. The cards and questions: the colour question's four grape and appellation pairs are of one kind, with Cerasuolo di Vittoria the near miss explained; the 1997 question's three other years each named in the explanation.

emidio-pepe: the note is answered: the founder died on 28 July 2026 at 94 and is named with his dates (1932 to 2026). The why holds, with old vintages decanted by hand into a new bottle before release.

masciarelli: the note is answered in part: the label is Villa Gemma Montepulciano d'Abruzzo DOC Riserva by the house's sheets, and the founder carries his death alone (2008) for want of a birth year in two sources (52 or 53 at death).

illuminati: the why's Controguerra house of 1890 is true of the house and not of the place (Ripatransone until 1960); its founder of the Colline Teramane DOCG is borne out in spirit by AbruzzoWeb and Il Centro, which call Dino Illuminati the consortium's first president and the man behind Abruzzo's first DOCG. The note's first vintage of Zanna is still unfound; 1890 and the label are confirmed.

cataldi-madonna: the note is answered: the house names no flagship, one merchant names Tonì, and the label of the 2024 vintage reads Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo Superiore Terre Aquilane DOC while older ones read Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo DOC, so the record prints Cerasuolo d'Abruzzo alone.
